newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Poland sees $500 mln debt issue in 1998 - Belka.
newsitem.headline: Poland sees $500 mln debt issue in 1998 - Belka.

text.p: Poland has completed its borrowing plans in the international capital markets this year but the country is likely to launch a $500 million issue in 1998, Poland's Finance Minister Marek Belka said on Thursday.

"Next year, we will probably repeat the exercise with another $500 million issue," Belka, who is also Deputy Prime Minister, told Reuters in an interview at an eastern European summit meeting in this alpine city.
Poland last tapped the international capital market in June with a $400 million yankee bond issue which consisted of seven-year and 20-year bonds.
Asked whether a credit rating upgrade was likely this year, Belka responded: "Definitely. I think they (the rating agencies) are waiting for the Polish elections."
Poland is currently rated BBB- with a positive outlook by U.S. rating agency Standard & Poor's Corp and Baa3 by Moody's Investors Services Inc.
Belka declined to say what Poland's future plans were on buying back its Brady debt.
"We are looking for different options, but for obvious reasons I am not going to publicise any activities on this." -- Diane Craft, Salzburg newsroom +43-662 879 943
